cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: Every turn T2-T10 answers its predecessor: T4 grants T3's tests, T8 attacks T7's privacy test.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T5 introduces ordinary-Tuesday versus event; T6 and section E build tests on it.
cells.limitation: T3's concrete tests (renting, dating) are never revisited after the Tuesday reframe.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T1-T2 set real desire against peer ranking; T8-T9 examine whether social wanting is borrowed.
cells.limitation: Fear of drifting from friends as their lives change is never raised by any mind.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T6 adopts T5's Tuesday point; T9 narrows its claim after T8; section D keeps disputes open.
cells.limitation: The Experimenter's testing frame is challenged only once (T4) and becomes consensus by T6.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D untangles feeling behind from wanting the life, sharper than section A's framing.
cells.limitation: T10 claims the feeling of being behind fades on its own without support.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T2 restates T1's peer-pressure reading fairly before calling it unproven.
cells.limitation: T3 dismisses both prior views as armchair arguing without engaging T2's forecasting point.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T8 names T7's assumption that shared meaning is contamination and shows wanting disappears; T9 answers.
cells.limitation: T4's contamination objection is only partly answered; T5 redesigns tests but not observer effects.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: Veblen emulation, Gilbert surrogate advice, Ibarra test-and-learn paraphrased plausibly; extensions flagged in T6-T10.
cells.limitation: T8's social-happiness attribution to Gilbert is loose and unverified; suspected, not established.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: Section A separates known feeling from unknown cause; section D frames its question as not a conclusion.
cells.limitation: T1 asserts the user is scored on a game never joined as fact.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T9 'Accepted, and it narrows my claim'; T5 undercuts its own surrogate advice.
cells.limitation: T2's point that the user's doubt is itself a forecast is never answered by the Status Critic.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A names the ambiguity: hidden wish for milestones, reaction to peers, or both.
cells.limitation: Living with the feeling now, apart from diagnosing it, gets only T10's one line.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: The friends-as-audience detail drives T4's contamination worry and section E's friends'-reactions branch.
cells.limitation: T3's test list is generic and not shaped by anything the user said.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E treats doing nothing as legitimate, honouring the user's stated doubt about wanting milestones.
cells.limitation: What the user does want instead of these milestones is never asked.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: Section E asks whether any option carries a real deadline.
cells.limitation: T3 assumes the user is single and renting; neither was stated.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on whether pull appears on ordinary days or only imagining friends' reactions.
cells.limitation: Relationship status and age never become questions though T3's tests depend on them.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T9 offers witnessed-by-one versus keeping-pace motives; section D gives an answerable question.
cells.limitation: T1 states the ranking motive flatly before T2 corrects it.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T2 shows 'not sure I want' is itself a forecast; T6 exposes confirmation reading of tests.
cells.limitation: The schedule implied by 'behind' is only glancingly questioned via T1's scoreboard.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T9 separates being witnessed from keeping pace as distinct valued outcomes.
cells.limitation: Values the user might hold apart from these milestones (freedom, work) are never surfaced.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T1 and T4 name peer approval and social scoreboard without pathologising.
cells.limitation: Fear of being left alone as friends settle, or family expectation, never named.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section D: 'a question to try on, not a conclusion about you.'
cells.limitation: T1's verdict-style framing precedes the debate's later open stance.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Section E defines pursue deliberately, wait or do nothing, and cheap reversible tests.
cells.limitation: What pursuing one deliberately would concretely involve stays undefined.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: Section E notes some wants cannot wait, a cost of doing nothing.
cells.limitation: Costs of pursuing and of tests like dating seriously for a season (T3) are never stated.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: pull on ordinary days favours pursuing; pull only at friends' reactions favours waiting.
cells.limitation: 'A few months' and 'a season' (T3, T10) are not drawn from user facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section A names which-pull as the decisive unknown; section E adds deadlines.
cells.limitation: Minor unknowns are never explicitly set apart from the consequential ones.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Section E: talk with people about routine weeks and pre-decide what counts as yes.
cells.limitation: A trial living or dating arrangement (section E, T3) is heavier than 'cheap' suggests.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T8 'Social does not mean fake'; plain vocabulary throughout, no jargon.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T8 'That test' maps to T7; T6 'Tuesdays' maps to T5; T4 'tests' maps to T3.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Ten turns within range, each one move; sections D and E stay compact.
cells.limitation: Turn lengths across T1-T10 are near-identical, giving an even, unvaried pace.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Positions stay distinct: scoreboard (T1), forecasting error (T2), testing (T3); T9 marks its shift.
cells.limitation: All three minds share one calm analytic register; voices differ only by stance.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: No turn repeats a prior claim; T6 and T9 each add before moving on.
cells.limitation: Section D largely restates T10's two-question split.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T8 'you have defined wanting out of existence' raises real stakes for the privacy test.
cells.limitation: The sting of feeling behind is never voiced vividly; stakes stay intellectual.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T9 narrows its claim, citing T8's point that being witnessed is a genuine want.
cells.limitation: Only one real reversal; T4's grant and T5's self-undercut are small turns.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T3's brisk 'Cheap tests beat a perfect theory' gives the Experimenter some edge.
cells.limitation: Minds lack temperament or idiom; expression is uniformly measured across T1-T10.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T5's ordinary Tuesday versus wedding day; T1's scoreboard; T8 'Social does not mean fake.'
cells.limitation: No concrete scene or example beyond the apartment walk-through in T4.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T7's 'harder cut' and T8's rebuttal build to T9's concession.
cells.limitation: Intensity stays constant and analytic; no emotional rise or release across turns.

strengths: T8-T9: a named-assumption objection produces a traced, narrowing concession by the Status Critic.
T5's ordinary-Tuesday distinction is developed by T6 and anchors section E's observable conditions.
Section D and E offer reflection as questions the user can test, not verdicts about the user.
weaknesses: Section E and T3 treat testing and pursuing as near-costless; dating seriously for a season has real costs.
No mind raises fear of drifting from friends or what the user wants instead of these milestones.
All three minds speak in one measured analytic register with near-identical turn lengths.

symptoms.observed: Tests and pursuit carry no stated cost; serious dating framed as cheap.
symptoms.evidence: Rent near a lively neighborhood, date seriously for a season

symptoms.observed: Feeling behind read only as ranking or wish; fear of losing friends never raised.
symptoms.evidence: Wanting to keep pace with a group is a ranking.

symptoms.observed: Tests assume single renter; relationship status and age never asked or branched.
symptoms.evidence: date seriously for a season, price a mortgage honestly

symptoms.observed: Test durations of a season or a few months not drawn from user facts.
symptoms.evidence: And if a season of trying shows no pull

symptoms.observed: Three minds share one calm analytic register; differ by stance only.
symptoms.evidence: Careful, that story is too convenient.

findings.description: Attributions to Veblen, Gilbert and Ibarra are paraphrases flagged as unverified; they match general knowledge of the books.
Claim that the feeling of being behind fades on its own once the second question is answered is asserted without support.
Attributing the point that much of happiness depends on other people to Stumbling on Happiness is loose; the turn flags the application as its own.

rubric_fit_notes: The situation gives few facts, so C3.2 and C3.4 are rated on restraint and use of the friends detail.
The self_reflection subtype fits criterion 4 well; criterion 5's decision is soft (pursue, wait, test) and was read as such.
question_type_note: Read as a decision question with a self-reflection subtype, so pursue, wait and test count as the options and introspective but observable signals count as decisive conditions.
